questions.stem: Christians believe that God is the Supreme Being who
options: was created by the first human beings
created heaven and earth and everything in them
is one of many equal gods
questions.explanation: Christians teach that God is the Creator of all things and is above everything He made (Genesis 1:1).

questions.stem: When we say that God is omnipotent, we mean that He is
questions.explanation: Omnipotent means having all power; nothing is too hard for God.

questions.stem: The belief that God is present everywhere at the same time is described as
questions.explanation: Omnipresent means present everywhere; Psalm 139 says we cannot hide from God anywhere.

questions.stem: Chiamaka says, "God knows what I am thinking even before I speak." Which attribute of God is she describing?
questions.explanation: Omniscience means God knows all things, including our thoughts.

questions.topic: Names of God in different Nigerian languages
questions.stem: In Yoruba, God is commonly called
questions.explanation: Olodumare (also Olorun) is the Yoruba name for the Supreme God.

questions.topic: Names of God in different Nigerian languages
questions.stem: The Igbo name for God which means "the Great God" or "Supreme God" is
questions.explanation: Chukwu comes from "Chi" (God/spirit) and "ukwu" (great).

questions.topic: Names of God in different Nigerian languages
questions.stem: Which of these is a Hausa name for God?
questions.explanation: Ubangiji (also Allah) is used for God by Hausa speakers.

questions.stem: According to Genesis 1, what did God create on the first day?
questions.explanation: On the first day God said, "Let there be light," and separated light from darkness.

questions.stem: On which day of creation did God make the sun, moon and stars?
questions.explanation: Genesis 1:14-19 records the creation of the great lights on the fourth day.

questions.stem: What did God do on the seventh day after finishing His work of creation?
options: He rested and blessed the day
questions.explanation: God rested on the seventh day, blessed it and made it holy (Genesis 2:2-3).

questions.stem: In the creation account, what did God create on the second day?
questions.explanation: On the second day God made the firmament to separate the waters above from the waters below.

questions.stem: According to Genesis 2, God formed the first man from
questions.explanation: God formed man from dust and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life (Genesis 2:7).

questions.stem: The Bible says God created human beings "in His own image". This means human beings
options: share some qualities of God such as the ability to think, love and choose
look exactly like God in physical shape
are equal to God in power
questions.explanation: Being made in God's image means we reflect some of His qualities and have special dignity.

questions.stem: God gave human beings dominion over the earth. This means they should
options: destroy plants and animals they do not need
care for and manage God's creation responsibly
leave the earth without any care
questions.explanation: Dominion is responsible stewardship: humans are caretakers of God's creation (Genesis 1:28).

questions.stem: "The heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament sheweth his handywork" is found in
questions.explanation: Psalm 19:1 is a song of praise about God's creation.

questions.stem: Christians sing songs about creation mainly to
options: show that human beings made the world
praise God for the wonderful things He made
questions.explanation: Creation songs, like many psalms, give glory and thanks to God the Creator.

questions.stem: In Christian teaching, marriage is
options: a business agreement that ends after a few years
a lifelong union between one man and one woman
a union between two families only, without the couple
an arrangement for only rich people
questions.explanation: Christian marriage joins a man and a woman as one flesh for life (Genesis 2:24).

questions.topic: Sharing God's creative activities through marriage
questions.stem: How do human beings share in God's creative activity through marriage?
questions.explanation: God blessed Adam and Eve and told them to be fruitful and multiply (Genesis 1:28).

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT a purpose of Christian marriage?
options: Gaining wealth from the bride price
questions.explanation: God said it is not good for man to be alone; marriage is for companionship, mutual help and children, not for profit.

questions.stem: Human beings share in God's creative work by using their God-given intelligence to
options: invent useful things like the telephone and computer
make rain fall whenever they like
questions.explanation: Inventions show human creativity, which comes from God.

questions.stem: Which statement best shows the Christian view of human inventions?
options: Inventions prove that human beings no longer need God
All inventions are evil and should be avoided
Only church leaders may use inventions
Inventions should be used to improve life and honour God, not to harm others
questions.explanation: God gives human beings wisdom; inventions should be used responsibly for good.

questions.topic: Biblical account of the first human disobedience
questions.stem: God told Adam not to eat from the
options: tree of the knowledge of good and evil
questions.explanation: God forbade them to eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil (Genesis 2:17).

questions.topic: Biblical account of the first human disobedience
questions.stem: Who tempted Eve to eat the forbidden fruit?
questions.explanation: The serpent deceived Eve into eating the fruit (Genesis 3:1-6).

questions.topic: Consequences of Adam and Eve's disobedience
questions.stem: Which of these was a consequence of Adam and Eve's disobedience?
options: They were given a new garden
They were driven out of the Garden of Eden
They were made rulers of Egypt
questions.explanation: After their sin, God sent them out of Eden (Genesis 3:23).

questions.topic: Consequences of Adam and Eve's disobedience
questions.stem: According to Genesis 3, the punishment for the man after the fall was that
options: he would crawl on his belly
he would work hard on the ground to get food
he would become a slave in Egypt
questions.explanation: God said the ground was cursed and man would eat by the sweat of his face.

questions.topic: Acts of disobedience and their consequences
questions.stem: King Saul disobeyed God by sparing King Agag and the best animals of the Amalekites. What was the result?
options: Saul was made king over all nations
questions.explanation: Samuel told Saul that because he rejected God's word, God had rejected him as king (1 Samuel 15).

questions.topic: Acts of disobedience and their consequences
questions.stem: Tunde was told not to swim in the river during the flood but he did and nearly drowned. This story teaches that
options: disobedience can lead to danger and suffering
parents do not care about children
questions.explanation: Like Adam and Eve, disobeying good instructions often brings painful results.

questions.stem: Reconciliation means
options: restoring a broken relationship between people
refusing to talk to an offender
questions.explanation: Reconciliation is making peace and restoring friendship after a quarrel.

questions.stem: Which of these is necessary for true reconciliation?
options: Confessing the wrong and being willing to forgive
Insisting that only the other person is wrong
Reporting the matter to everyone in the village
Waiting for the offender to suffer first
questions.explanation: Reconciliation needs repentance, confession and forgiveness from both sides.

questions.stem: Jacob was afraid of his brother Esau, whom he had cheated. When they met, Esau
options: attacked him with four hundred men
ran to meet him, embraced and kissed him
took all his cattle by force
questions.explanation: Esau forgave Jacob and embraced him; their relationship was restored (Genesis 33:4).

questions.stem: Joseph forgave his brothers who had sold him into slavery. What did he say to them?
options: "I will sell you into slavery too"
"Go back to Canaan and never return"
"You meant evil against me, but God meant it for good"
questions.explanation: Joseph saw God's plan in his suffering and forgave his brothers (Genesis 50:20).

questions.stem: A family made up of a father, a mother and their children only is called
questions.explanation: The nuclear family is the small family unit of parents and their children.

questions.stem: Emeka lives with his parents, grandparents, uncles and cousins in one compound. This is
questions.explanation: An extended family includes relatives beyond parents and children.

questions.stem: Your father's brother is your
questions.explanation: The brother of either parent is an uncle.

questions.topic: Roles of members of the family
questions.stem: According to Ephesians 6:1, children should
options: leave home as soon as possible
obey their parents in the Lord
questions.explanation: Paul wrote, "Children, obey your parents in the Lord: for this is right."

questions.topic: Roles of members of the family
questions.stem: Which of these is a duty of parents to their children?
options: Training them in the way they should go
Refusing to send them to school
questions.explanation: Proverbs 22:6 tells parents to train up a child in the way he should go.

questions.topic: Concept of a good family name
questions.stem: "A good name is rather to be chosen than great riches." This saying from Proverbs 22:1 teaches that
options: rich people always have good names
a good reputation is more valuable than wealth
wealth gives a person a good name
questions.explanation: Honesty and good behaviour build a family name that is worth more than money.

questions.topic: Concept of a good family name
questions.stem: Which behaviour helps to protect a good family name?
questions.explanation: Good conduct by each member keeps the family's name respected.

questions.topic: Names and members of the school
questions.stem: The head of a secondary school who oversees all the teachers and students is the
questions.explanation: The principal leads the school community.

questions.stem: Which person would be the best choice as a friend at school?
options: Ngozi, who is honest, kind and studies hard
questions.explanation: Good friends have good character; "Evil communications corrupt good manners" (1 Corinthians 15:33).

questions.stem: In the Bible, Jonathan was a faithful friend to
questions.explanation: Jonathan loved David as his own soul and protected him from Saul (1 Samuel 18-20).

questions.stem: Jonathan showed true friendship to David mainly by
options: warning David about Saul's plan to kill him
questions.explanation: Jonathan risked his father's anger to warn and save David (1 Samuel 20).

questions.stem: Rehoboam lost ten tribes of Israel because he
options: listened to the old men's advice
followed the harsh advice of his young friends
questions.explanation: Rehoboam rejected the elders' counsel and listened to his peers, so Israel rebelled (1 Kings 12).

questions.stem: Which of these is a likely effect of keeping bad friends?
options: Being led into wrong behaviour such as drug abuse
questions.explanation: Bad company can lead young people into crime, drugs and failure.

questions.stem: Which of these is a traditional community leader in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Traditional rulers such as the Oba, Obi or Emir lead their communities.

questions.topic: Ways of sustaining relationship in the community
questions.stem: Which of these helps to keep good relationships in a community?
options: Taking part in communal work like clearing drainages
questions.explanation: Working together and respecting others builds peace in the community.

questions.stem: The early Christians in Acts 2:42 continued steadfastly in
options: the apostles' teaching, fellowship, breaking of bread and prayers
questions.explanation: Fellowship, teaching, breaking bread and prayer bound church members together.

questions.stem: Which of these is a way Christians relate with God?
questions.explanation: Prayer is talking with God; Christians also relate with Him through worship and Bible reading.

questions.stem: God called Samuel three times while he was sleeping in the temple. This shows that God can speak to people
questions.explanation: God spoke to young Samuel by calling his name (1 Samuel 3).

questions.stem: Joseph, the husband of Mary, was told in a dream to flee to Egypt. This shows that God sometimes speaks through
questions.explanation: God warned Joseph in a dream to take the child and flee (Matthew 2:13).

questions.topic: Ways of maintaining good relationship with God
questions.stem: Which of these BEST helps a Christian to maintain a good relationship with God?
options: Going to church only at Christmas
Giving money while living in sin
Regular prayer, obedience to His word and repentance from sin
questions.explanation: A close relationship with God requires obedience, prayer and a repentant heart.

questions.stem: Obedience means
options: doing what one is told by a rightful authority
questions.explanation: To obey is to carry out instructions from God, parents or lawful authorities.

questions.stem: God called Abram to leave his country and go to a land He would show him. Abram left from
questions.explanation: Abram departed from Haran at 75 years old (Genesis 12:4).

questions.stem: Abraham's greatest test of obedience was when God asked him to
options: offer his son Isaac as a sacrifice
questions.explanation: Abraham was ready to offer Isaac, and God provided a ram instead (Genesis 22).

questions.stem: Because Abraham obeyed God, God promised that
options: he would become the father of many nations
questions.explanation: God promised to make Abraham a great nation and bless all families of the earth through him.

questions.stem: Which of these is an example of political freedom?
options: Citizens voting freely for their leaders
questions.explanation: Political freedom is the right to take part in choosing how one is governed.

questions.stem: God called Moses from
options: a burning bush that was not consumed
questions.explanation: God spoke to Moses from the burning bush at Mount Horeb (Exodus 3).

questions.stem: Moses complained that he was slow of speech. Who did God appoint to speak for him?
questions.explanation: God appointed Aaron, Moses' brother, to be his spokesman (Exodus 4:14-16).

questions.topic: Deborah and Barak lead their people to freedom
questions.stem: Deborah and Barak led Israel to victory over the army of Jabin, whose commander was
questions.explanation: Sisera, Jabin's commander, was defeated; Jael later killed him (Judges 4).

questions.topic: Deborah and Barak lead their people to freedom
questions.stem: Deborah was a prophetess and a
questions.explanation: Deborah judged Israel and sat under a palm tree to settle disputes (Judges 4:4-5).

questions.stem: Service means
options: working to help others or God without seeking selfish gain
forcing others to work for you
questions.explanation: Service is giving one's time and talent for the good of others.

questions.topic: Examples of people who served in the Bible
questions.stem: Which of these served her mother-in-law faithfully after her husband died?
questions.explanation: Ruth stayed with Naomi and said, "Thy people shall be my people" (Ruth 1:16).

questions.topic: Lessons from the service of Joseph and Ruth
questions.stem: Joseph served faithfully in Potiphar's house and later in prison. A lesson from his life is that
options: one should serve only when watched
faithful service is rewarded by God in due time
questions.explanation: Joseph suffered but God later raised him to be governor of Egypt.

questions.stem: Samuel served in the temple under Eli from childhood. What did his mother Hannah do to bring this about?
options: She sent him to Egypt to learn
She sold him to the priest
She asked King Saul to employ him
She dedicated him to the Lord as she had vowed
questions.explanation: Hannah vowed to give her son to the Lord and brought him to Eli at Shiloh (1 Samuel 1).

questions.stem: Which of these is a common problem people face in service?
questions.explanation: Those who serve often face ingratitude, misunderstanding and hardship.

questions.stem: Ruth was rewarded for her loyal service when she
options: married Boaz and became an ancestor of King David
questions.explanation: Ruth married Boaz; their son Obed was David's grandfather (Ruth 4:17).

questions.topic: King David obeys God's call to repentance
questions.stem: Which prophet confronted King David after his sin with Bathsheba?
questions.explanation: Nathan told David the parable of the poor man's lamb and said, "Thou art the man" (2 Samuel 12).

questions.topic: King David obeys God's call to repentance
questions.stem: David's response when confronted with his sin was
options: "I am the king; no one can judge me"
questions.explanation: David confessed his sin humbly; Psalm 51 is linked to his repentance.

questions.topic: The people of Nineveh repented of their sins
questions.stem: God sent the prophet Jonah to preach to the people of
questions.explanation: Jonah was sent to warn Nineveh, the great city (Jonah 1:2).

questions.topic: The people of Nineveh repented of their sins
questions.stem: When Nineveh heard Jonah's message, the people
options: fasted, wore sackcloth and turned from their evil ways
questions.explanation: God saw their repentance and did not destroy the city (Jonah 3:5-10).

questions.topic: John the Baptist calls for repentance
questions.stem: John the Baptist preached, "Repent ye: for
options: the kingdom of heaven is at hand"
questions.explanation: John preached repentance in the wilderness of Judea (Matthew 3:2).

questions.stem: What happened to the people of Noah's day who refused to repent?
options: They were destroyed by the flood
questions.explanation: Only Noah and his family were saved; the unrepentant perished (Genesis 7).

questions.stem: In Luke 13:3 Jesus warned, "Except ye repent, ye shall all likewise perish." He said this to teach that
options: disasters happen only to the worst sinners
everyone needs to turn from sin, not only those who suffer disasters
questions.explanation: Jesus taught that all people are sinners and must repent.

questions.stem: Which angel announced to Mary that she would give birth to Jesus?
questions.explanation: The angel Gabriel was sent to Mary in Nazareth (Luke 1:26-31).

questions.stem: Mary responded to the angel's message by saying
options: "Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it unto me according to thy word"
"Show me a sign from heaven first"
questions.explanation: Mary humbly accepted God's will (Luke 1:38).

questions.stem: Jesus was born in
questions.explanation: Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea (Luke 2:4-7; Matthew 2:1).

questions.stem: Why did Joseph and Mary travel to Bethlehem before Jesus was born?
options: To register in a census ordered by Caesar Augustus
questions.explanation: Everyone went to his own city to be taxed (registered); Joseph was of the house of David (Luke 2:1-4).

questions.stem: The angel told the shepherds that they would find the baby
options: sitting on a throne in Jerusalem
in the temple with the priests
wrapped in swaddling clothes, lying in a manger
in a boat on the sea
questions.explanation: This was the sign given to the shepherds (Luke 2:12).

questions.topic: The visit of the wise men
questions.stem: The gifts the wise men brought to the child Jesus were
questions.explanation: The wise men opened their treasures and offered gold, frankincense and myrrh (Matthew 2:11).

questions.topic: The visit of the wise men
questions.stem: Why did the wise men not return to Herod after seeing Jesus?
options: They were warned by God in a dream
questions.explanation: God warned them in a dream, so they went home by another way (Matthew 2:12).

questions.topic: The values of virginity before marriage
questions.stem: Which of these is a benefit of keeping one's virginity until marriage?
options: Avoiding unwanted pregnancy and sexually transmitted infections
questions.explanation: Chastity protects young people's health, education and honour, as Mary's purity is admired.

questions.stem: When Jesus was presented in the temple, His parents offered
options: a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons
questions.explanation: They offered the sacrifice allowed by the law of the Lord (Luke 2:24).

questions.stem: Simeon had been told by the Holy Spirit that he would not die until he
questions.explanation: Simeon took the child in his arms and blessed God (Luke 2:26-28).

questions.stem: Anna, who spoke about the child Jesus in the temple, was
options: the mother of John the Baptist
the wife of the high priest
an elderly prophetess who served God with fasting and prayer
questions.explanation: Anna, daughter of Phanuel, was a widow who worshipped in the temple night and day (Luke 2:36-38).

questions.stem: At the age of twelve, Jesus was found by His parents in the temple
options: sitting among the teachers, listening and asking questions
questions.explanation: After three days they found Him among the doctors (teachers) of the law (Luke 2:46).

questions.stem: After His parents found Him in the temple, Jesus
options: stayed in Jerusalem for a year
went down with them to Nazareth and was subject to them
questions.explanation: Luke 2:51 says He was obedient to His parents.

questions.stem: Jesus said, "Whosoever shall do the will of God, the same is my brother, and my sister, and mother." He meant that
options: all who obey God belong to His spiritual family
only His relatives would be saved
questions.explanation: Jesus widened the idea of family to include all who do God's will (Mark 3:35).

questions.topic: Account of the baptism of Jesus Christ
questions.stem: Jesus was baptised by John in the River
questions.explanation: Jesus came from Galilee to the Jordan to be baptised by John (Matthew 3:13).

questions.topic: Account of the baptism of Jesus Christ
questions.stem: After the baptism of Jesus, the Spirit of God came down upon Him like
questions.explanation: The heavens opened and the Spirit descended like a dove (Matthew 3:16).

questions.topic: Significance of the baptism of Jesus
questions.stem: The voice from heaven at Jesus' baptism said, "This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased." This showed that
options: Jesus needed to repent of sins
God approved of Jesus and confirmed Him as His Son
questions.explanation: The voice publicly confirmed Jesus' identity and mission.

questions.topic: Importance of baptism in the life of a Christian
questions.stem: For Christians, baptism is a sign of
options: cleansing from sin and entry into the Christian community
questions.explanation: Baptism symbolises new life in Christ and membership of the Church.

questions.topic: Account of the temptation of Jesus Christ
questions.stem: Before He was tempted by the devil, Jesus fasted in the wilderness for
questions.explanation: Jesus fasted forty days and forty nights (Matthew 4:2).

questions.topic: Account of the temptation of Jesus Christ
questions.stem: In the first temptation, the devil asked Jesus to
questions.explanation: Jesus replied, "Man shall not live by bread alone" (Matthew 4:3-4).

questions.topic: Significance of the temptation of Jesus
questions.stem: In each temptation, Jesus answered the devil by
questions.explanation: Jesus said "It is written" each time, showing the power of God's word.

questions.stem: A good way for a Christian to overcome temptation is to
options: keep company with people who do wrong
pray and avoid situations that lead to sin
questions.explanation: Prayer, Bible study and avoiding bad situations help to resist temptation.

questions.topic: Temptations in the life of a Christian
questions.stem: Kemi finds ₦5,000 that a classmate dropped and is tempted to keep it. What should she do?
options: Keep it and tell no one
Return it to the owner or give it to the teacher
questions.explanation: Honesty means returning what belongs to others.

questions.topic: Jesus calls His first four disciples
questions.stem: The first four disciples Jesus called by the Sea of Galilee were
questions.explanation: Peter, Andrew, James and John were fishermen (Mark 1:16-20).

questions.topic: Jesus calls His first four disciples
questions.stem: Which pair of brothers were the sons of Zebedee?
questions.explanation: James and John, sons of Zebedee, left their father in the boat to follow Jesus.

questions.stem: Which of the twelve apostles was a tax collector before he followed Jesus?
questions.explanation: Jesus called Matthew from the tax office (Matthew 9:9).

questions.topic: What it takes to be a disciple of Jesus Christ
questions.stem: Jesus said, "If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me." This means a disciple must
options: be willing to make sacrifices for Christ
questions.explanation: Discipleship requires self-denial and commitment (Matthew 16:24).

questions.stem: When Jesus said "I will make you fishers of men", He meant that the disciples would
questions.explanation: They would win people for the kingdom of God.

questions.topic: Mission of the twelve apostles and the seventy disciples
questions.stem: When Jesus sent out the seventy, He sent them
questions.explanation: Jesus sent the seventy two by two ahead of Him (Luke 10:1).

questions.topic: Preaching the Gospel and healing the sick
questions.stem: Jesus told the twelve to take nothing for their journey. This taught them to
options: depend on God to provide for them
questions.explanation: They were to trust God, who would provide through those who received them (Luke 9:3).

questions.topic: Outcome of the mission of the twelve and seventy disciples
questions.stem: The seventy returned with joy saying, "Lord, even the devils are subject unto us through thy name." Jesus told them to rejoice rather because
options: their names were written in heaven
questions.explanation: Jesus said salvation is greater cause for joy than power (Luke 10:20).

questions.stem: "Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall
options: be called the children of God"
questions.explanation: Matthew 5:9 promises that peacemakers will be called children of God.

questions.stem: According to the Beatitudes, who shall inherit the earth?
questions.explanation: "Blessed are the meek: for they shall inherit the earth" (Matthew 5:5).

questions.topic: Teachings of the Sermon on the Mount
questions.stem: In the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus taught His followers to
options: take an eye for an eye
love their enemies and pray for those who persecute them
questions.explanation: Jesus taught love even for enemies (Matthew 5:44).

questions.topic: Teachings of the Sermon on the Mount
questions.stem: Jesus said His followers are "the salt of the earth" and "the light of the world". This means Christians should
options: influence society for good through their good works
questions.explanation: Like salt and light, Christians should preserve and brighten society (Matthew 5:13-16).

questions.stem: A parable is
options: an earthly story with a heavenly meaning
questions.explanation: Jesus used everyday stories to teach spiritual truths.

questions.topic: Parables about the Kingdom: the Sower
questions.stem: In the Parable of the Sower, the seed that fell on good soil represents
options: people who forget the word quickly
people choked by worries of life
people who hear the word, understand it and bear fruit
questions.explanation: The good soil stands for those who hear and obey God's word (Matthew 13:23).

questions.stem: In the Parable of the Wheat and the Tares, the tares were allowed to grow with the wheat until
questions.explanation: At harvest the tares would be gathered and burned; this pictures the final judgement (Matthew 13:30).

questions.stem: In the Parable of the Prodigal Son, when the son returned home, his father
options: made him a slave for life
ran to embrace him and threw a feast
questions.explanation: The father's welcome shows God's love for repentant sinners (Luke 15:20-24).

questions.stem: In the Parable of the Lost Sheep, the shepherd left the ninety-nine sheep to
options: look for the one that was lost
questions.explanation: God seeks every lost person (Luke 15:4).

questions.topic: Parables about our attitude to earthly possessions
questions.stem: In the Parable of the Rich Fool, the rich man planned to
options: pull down his barns and build bigger ones
give his crops to the poor
sell his land to the temple
share his wealth with his brothers
questions.explanation: God called him a fool because he was not rich towards God (Luke 12:16-21).

questions.stem: In the Parable of the Talents, the servant who received one talent was punished because he
options: hid it in the ground instead of using it
questions.explanation: The lesson is that we must use our God-given abilities well (Matthew 25:24-30).

questions.stem: The Parable of the Unforgiving Servant teaches that
options: those who have been forgiven must forgive others
questions.explanation: Jesus warned that God will not forgive those who refuse to forgive (Matthew 18:35).

questions.stem: A miracle is
options: a story told to teach a lesson
an extraordinary event that shows the power of God
questions.explanation: Miracles are wonders beyond natural explanation, done by God's power.

questions.stem: Jesus' first miracle at the wedding in Cana of Galilee was
questions.explanation: John 2:1-11 records this as His first sign.

questions.stem: When Jesus calmed the storm, He rebuked the wind and said to the sea,
questions.explanation: The wind ceased and there was a great calm (Mark 4:39).

questions.stem: In the feeding of the four thousand, how many baskets of leftovers were gathered?
questions.explanation: They took up seven baskets of broken pieces (Mark 8:8); at the feeding of the five thousand it was twelve.

questions.stem: When Peter walked on the water towards Jesus, he began to sink because
options: Jesus told him to go back
he saw the strong wind and became afraid
he was carrying a heavy load
questions.explanation: Jesus said, "O thou of little faith, wherefore didst thou doubt?" (Matthew 14:30-31).

questions.stem: Blind Bartimaeus received his sight near
questions.explanation: Bartimaeus sat by the roadside near Jericho (Mark 10:46-52).

questions.stem: Jesus raised Lazarus from the dead in
questions.explanation: Lazarus of Bethany, brother of Mary and Martha, was raised after four days (John 11).

questions.stem: Jesus raised the only son of a widow at the gate of the city of
questions.explanation: He touched the bier and said, "Young man, I say unto thee, Arise" (Luke 7:11-15).

questions.stem: Jesus told Peter to find money for the temple tax
options: in the mouth of a fish
in the treasury of the temple
questions.explanation: Peter found a coin in the mouth of the first fish he caught (Matthew 17:27).

questions.topic: Jesus' attitude to civil and religious laws
questions.stem: "Render therefore unto Caesar the things which are Caesar's; and unto God the things that are God's." This teaches that Christians should
options: obey the government and also be faithful to God
questions.explanation: Jesus taught duties to both the state and God (Matthew 22:21).

questions.stem: Jesus said the first and greatest commandment is to
options: love the Lord your God with all your heart, soul and mind
questions.explanation: The second is to love your neighbour as yourself (Matthew 22:37-39).

questions.stem: According to 1 Corinthians 13, love
questions.explanation: Paul describes love as patient, kind, not envious or proud.

questions.stem: Jesus rode into Jerusalem on
questions.explanation: He rode on a colt while crowds cried "Hosanna" (Mark 11:7-9).

questions.stem: At the Last Supper, Jesus took bread, blessed it and said,
questions.explanation: The bread represents His body given for us (Matthew 26:26).

questions.stem: Judas Iscariot betrayed Jesus for
questions.explanation: The chief priests paid Judas thirty pieces of silver (Matthew 26:15).

questions.stem: Judas showed the soldiers which man was Jesus by
questions.explanation: The kiss was the agreed sign (Mark 14:44).

questions.stem: Peter denied Jesus three times before
questions.explanation: Jesus had predicted Peter's denial before the cock crowed (Matthew 26:34, 75).

questions.topic: Instances that can lead a Christian to deny Christ
questions.stem: Which situation is MOST likely to tempt a Christian to deny Christ, as Peter did?
options: Fear of being mocked or punished for one's faith
questions.explanation: Peter denied Jesus out of fear; peer pressure and persecution can lead people to deny their faith.

questions.stem: Jesus was crucified at a place called
questions.explanation: Golgotha means "place of a skull" (John 19:17).

questions.stem: Which of these did Jesus say on the cross?
options: "Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do"
questions.explanation: Jesus prayed for those who crucified Him (Luke 23:34).

questions.stem: At the moment Jesus died, the veil of the temple
options: was torn in two from top to bottom
questions.explanation: The torn veil shows that the way to God was opened (Matthew 27:51).

questions.stem: Jesus' body was buried in a new tomb belonging to
questions.explanation: Joseph of Arimathea asked Pilate for the body and laid it in his own new tomb (Matthew 27:57-60).

questions.stem: Jesus rose from the dead on
questions.explanation: He rose on the first day of the week, the third day after His death.

questions.stem: The risen Jesus appeared to two disciples on the road to
questions.explanation: They recognised Him when He broke bread (Luke 24:13-31).

questions.stem: Thomas refused to believe in the resurrection until he could
options: see and touch the nail marks in Jesus' hands
questions.explanation: When Jesus appeared, Thomas said, "My Lord and my God" (John 20:25-28).

questions.topic: Significance of Jesus' resurrection to Christians
questions.stem: The resurrection of Jesus is important to Christians because it
options: proves that death is the end
means Christians will never fall sick
gives hope of eternal life and shows His victory over death
shows that the Romans were powerful
questions.explanation: Paul says if Christ is not risen, our faith is in vain (1 Corinthians 15:14-20).

questions.stem: In the Great Commission, Jesus told His disciples to
options: go and make disciples of all nations
questions.explanation: Matthew 28:19 commands them to teach and baptise all nations.

questions.stem: Jesus ascended into heaven from a place near
options: Bethany, on the Mount of Olives
questions.explanation: Luke 24:50-51 and Acts 1:12 place the ascension near Bethany at the Mount of Olives.

questions.topic: Signs that will accompany those who spread the gospel
questions.stem: According to Mark 16:17-18, which sign would follow those who believe?
options: They would cast out devils and lay hands on the sick
questions.explanation: Jesus listed casting out devils, speaking in new tongues and healing the sick.

questions.stem: Jesus told the disciples to wait in Jerusalem until they received
options: power from on high (the Holy Spirit)
questions.explanation: Luke 24:49 and Acts 1:4-8 record this promise.

questions.topic: The coming of the Holy Spirit
questions.stem: The Holy Spirit came upon the disciples on the day of
questions.explanation: Acts 2:1-4 describes the coming of the Spirit at Pentecost.

questions.topic: The coming of the Holy Spirit
questions.stem: On the day of Pentecost, the Holy Spirit appeared as
options: tongues like fire resting on each of them
questions.explanation: They were filled with the Spirit and spoke in other tongues (Acts 2:3-4).

questions.topic: Peter's first speech and its effect
questions.stem: After Peter's speech on the day of Pentecost, about how many people were added to the believers?
questions.explanation: Acts 2:41 says about three thousand souls were added that day.

questions.topic: Social and religious life of the Early Church
questions.stem: The early believers in Jerusalem
options: kept all their wealth to themselves
had all things in common and shared with anyone in need
questions.explanation: They sold possessions and shared according to need (Acts 2:44-45).

questions.stem: Seven deacons were chosen in the early Church to
options: serve tables and care for widows in the daily distribution
questions.explanation: The apostles wanted to devote themselves to prayer and the word (Acts 6:1-4).

questions.stem: Which of these was one of the seven deacons?
questions.explanation: Stephen, full of faith and the Holy Spirit, was among the seven (Acts 6:5).

questions.topic: Comparison of the Early Church to the present Church
questions.stem: Which practice of the Early Church is often missing in many churches today?
options: Sharing possessions so that no member lacked anything
questions.explanation: The Early Church shared so fully that "neither was there any among them that lacked" (Acts 4:34).

questions.stem: Peter and John were arrested after they
options: healed a lame man at the Beautiful Gate and preached about Jesus
questions.explanation: The healing and preaching angered the priests and Sadducees (Acts 3-4).

questions.stem: Stephen, the first Christian martyr, was killed by
questions.explanation: Stephen was stoned and prayed for his killers (Acts 7:59-60).

questions.topic: Persecution of the Church by Saul
questions.stem: Saul was travelling to which city to arrest Christians when he was converted?
questions.explanation: A light from heaven shone on him on the road to Damascus (Acts 9:3).

questions.stem: James the brother of John was killed with the sword by
questions.explanation: Herod killed James with the sword (Acts 12:1-2).

questions.stem: Simon the magician offered the apostles money in order to
options: receive the power to give the Holy Spirit
questions.explanation: Peter rebuked him: the gift of God cannot be bought with money (Acts 8:18-20).

questions.stem: Peter raised Tabitha (Dorcas) from the dead at
questions.explanation: Dorcas, known for good works, was raised at Joppa (Acts 9:36-41).

questions.stem: The conversion of Cornelius was important because it showed that
options: Christians must keep all Jewish food laws
the gospel is for Gentiles as well as Jews
questions.explanation: Peter said God shows no partiality (Acts 10:34-35).

questions.topic: Peter's divine release from prison and death of Herod
questions.stem: Peter was released from prison by
questions.explanation: An angel woke him, his chains fell off and the iron gate opened (Acts 12:7-10).

questions.topic: Paul's teachings on dignity of labour, obedience and love
questions.stem: Paul wrote, "If any would not work, neither should he
questions.explanation: 2 Thessalonians 3:10 teaches the dignity of labour.

questions.stem: Which of these is an example of skilled manual work?
questions.explanation: Carpentry is honest skilled work; Jesus Himself was a carpenter.

questions.topic: Why people should do their work with honour
questions.stem: Paul taught Christians to do their work "heartily, as to the Lord". This means they should
options: work only when the boss is watching
work sincerely and well, as if working for God
questions.explanation: Colossians 3:23 teaches diligence in every task.

questions.stem: In Romans 13, Paul teaches that Christians should obey governing authorities because
options: authorities are ordained by God to maintain order
questions.explanation: Romans 13:1 says the powers that be are ordained of God.

questions.topic: Paul's arrival at Jerusalem and arrest
questions.stem: Paul was arrested in Jerusalem after some Jews accused him of
questions.explanation: They thought he had brought Trophimus, a Greek, into the temple (Acts 21:28-29).

questions.topic: Paul before the Jewish Council and the plot to kill him
questions.stem: The plot of more than forty men to kill Paul was discovered by
questions.explanation: Paul's nephew told the commander, who sent Paul to Caesarea (Acts 23:16-24).

questions.topic: Paul before Roman Governors and his appeal to Rome
questions.stem: Before Governor Festus, Paul said, "I appeal unto Caesar". He did this because
options: he wanted to visit his family in Rome
as a Roman citizen he had the right to be tried by Caesar
questions.explanation: Paul used his right as a Roman citizen (Acts 25:11).

questions.topic: The Great Commission (growth of the Church)
questions.stem: In Acts 1:8, Jesus said His disciples would be His witnesses in Jerusalem, Judea, Samaria and
options: to the ends of the earth
questions.explanation: The Church grew outwards from Jerusalem to the whole world.

questions.topic: Marks of growth in the Church
questions.stem: Which of these is a sign that a church is growing?
options: Increase in the number of committed believers
questions.explanation: Growth is shown in numbers, faith and good works.

questions.stem: Which body brings together many Christian churches in Nigeria?
options: Nigerian Supreme Council for Islamic Affairs
questions.explanation: CAN is the umbrella body for Christian denominations in Nigeria.

questions.stem: Students from different churches meet on campus for joint Bible study and prayer. This is an example of
questions.explanation: Inter-denominational groups such as the Scripture Union bring Christians of many churches together.

questions.stem: Paul taught that "God loveth a
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 9:7 teaches that giving should be willing and joyful.

questions.stem: Jesus prayed for His followers "that they all may be one". This teaches Christians to
options: live in unity despite their different denominations
questions.explanation: John 17:21 records Jesus' prayer for unity.

questions.stem: A Christian living among people of other faiths should
options: show love, honesty and respect to everyone
questions.explanation: Christians are called to love their neighbours, whatever their faith.

questions.stem: Jesus taught that those who are persecuted for righteousness' sake should
options: rejoice, for great is their reward in heaven
questions.explanation: Matthew 5:10-12 promises a reward to the persecuted.

questions.stem: Daniel continued to pray to God even when King Darius's decree forbade it. This shows that a believer
options: respects rulers but obeys God when a law requires disobeying Him
questions.explanation: Daniel served the king faithfully yet stayed loyal to God (Daniel 6).

questions.stem: Peaceful co-existence means
options: living together in harmony despite differences
forcing others to share your religion
questions.explanation: It means people of different faiths and groups living peacefully together.

questions.topic: Ways of showing desire for peaceful co-existence
questions.stem: Which action promotes peaceful co-existence between Christians and Muslims in a community?
options: Destroying each other's places of worship
Refusing to trade with each other
Visiting and greeting each other during festivals
questions.explanation: Mutual respect and friendship encourage peace.

questions.topic: Origin of Christianity and Islam from Abraham
questions.stem: Christians and Muslims both regard Abraham as an ancestor of faith. According to the Bible, Abraham's son by Hagar was
questions.explanation: Ishmael was born to Hagar; Isaac was born to Sarah (Genesis 16; 21).

questions.topic: Origin of Christianity and Islam from Abraham
questions.stem: Why is Abraham important for peaceful co-existence between Christians and Muslims?
options: He founded the Church in Nigeria
Both religions trace their faith back to him, so they share a common heritage
questions.explanation: A shared ancestor in faith is a reason for mutual respect.

questions.stem: God is described as eternal. This means He
options: was born a long time ago
has no beginning and no end
questions.explanation: Psalm 90:2 says from everlasting to everlasting He is God.

questions.stem: On the third day of creation, God
options: gathered the waters to make dry land appear and made plants grow
questions.explanation: Dry land, seas and plants appeared on the third day (Genesis 1:9-13).

questions.stem: According to Genesis 2, God made Eve from
options: the dust of the river bank
questions.explanation: God caused a deep sleep to fall on Adam and made woman from his rib (Genesis 2:21-22).

questions.stem: What work did God give Adam in the Garden of Eden?
options: To tend and keep the garden and name the animals
To guard the gate with a sword
questions.explanation: Adam was to dress and keep the garden, and he named the creatures (Genesis 2:15, 19-20).

questions.stem: "Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh." This verse teaches that in marriage
options: parents must live with the couple
the man must forget his parents completely
a man may have many wives
husband and wife form a new, close and lasting union
questions.explanation: Genesis 2:24 stresses the unity and permanence of marriage.

questions.topic: Biblical account of the first human disobedience
questions.stem: When God asked Adam why he ate the fruit, Adam
options: blamed the woman God gave him
questions.explanation: Adam blamed Eve and Eve blamed the serpent (Genesis 3:12-13).

questions.topic: Acts of disobedience and their consequences
questions.stem: Lot's wife disobeyed the angels' instruction while fleeing from Sodom. What happened to her?
options: She became a pillar of salt
She was swallowed by the earth
questions.explanation: She looked back and became a pillar of salt (Genesis 19:26).

questions.topic: Acts of disobedience and their consequences
questions.stem: Because Moses struck the rock instead of speaking to it as God commanded, God said he would
options: not lead Israel into the Promised Land
questions.explanation: Moses and Aaron were not allowed to bring Israel into Canaan (Numbers 20:7-12).

questions.stem: Uche and Ifeanyi quarrelled over a football. The next day Uche apologised and they became friends again. This is an example of
questions.explanation: Restoring friendship after a quarrel is reconciliation.

questions.stem: Your mother's sister's daughter is your
questions.explanation: The children of your aunts and uncles are your cousins.

questions.stem: Which of these shows a person relating with God through worship?
options: Singing praises and giving thanks to God
questions.explanation: Worship includes praise, thanksgiving and prayer.

questions.stem: When Abraham obeyed God's call, he left his country with
options: his wife Sarai and his nephew Lot
questions.explanation: Abram took Sarai and Lot with him (Genesis 12:5).

questions.stem: God told Moses at the burning bush to take off his shoes because
options: the place where he stood was holy ground
questions.explanation: God's presence made the place holy (Exodus 3:5).

questions.stem: God called Moses to lead the Israelites out of slavery in
questions.explanation: God heard the cry of the Israelites in Egypt and sent Moses (Exodus 3:10).

questions.topic: Examples of people who served in the Bible
questions.stem: Who served as governor of Egypt and stored grain during seven years of plenty?
questions.explanation: Joseph prepared Egypt for the famine (Genesis 41).

questions.stem: After Joseph interpreted Pharaoh's dreams, Pharaoh rewarded him by
options: making him ruler over all the land of Egypt
questions.explanation: Pharaoh set Joseph over all Egypt and gave him his ring (Genesis 41:41-42).

questions.topic: The people of Nineveh repented of their sins
questions.stem: Jonah was angry when God spared Nineveh. God taught him a lesson using
options: a plant (gourd) that grew up and withered
questions.explanation: God showed that He cares for all people, even Israel's enemies (Jonah 4).

questions.topic: John the Baptist calls for repentance
questions.stem: John the Baptist told people who had two coats to
options: give one to the person who had none
questions.explanation: John taught that repentance shows in generous actions (Luke 3:11).
